items_missed: No agenda timeframe and no 'sound good?' confirmation — she gave the roadmap ('get your details, then I'll be discussing how our pricing works and then discuss your customized quote') but never set the 10-15 minute expectation or asked the customer to agree to it. The 10-15 minutes she did mention was the length of the virtual walkthrough, not the call.
Never said 'How are you today?' — opened straight into 'How can I help you today?'
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.

Got the customer's live yes on the virtual walkthrough and let it evaporate. Customer volunteered 'My daughter is home right now she can do it.' Therese answered 'I can definitely do that for you today... so we can schedule that today' and then never named a time, never sent the link, and closed with 'reply back to that email once you do have availability.' The walkthrough went from booked to homework in three sentences.
Never attempted to lock the move date. She opened by confirming Wednesday and Thursday availability, the customer said 'Yup' to both, and the ask never came — on a move happening THIS WEEK.
Never mentioned that no deposit is required.
No 'reply with any corrections' — the email ask was only about walkthrough availability, not verifying the details she collected.
No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email.
Never gave business hours or how to reach us.
Zero Save Your Ass content — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip, no 'does that make sense' close.
Collected stairs (3-story origin, 2-story destination) and never explained that stairs drive the clock on a time-based bill.
Collected the narrow townhome entry and street-only parking (no driveway) and never explained walk distance and access as time variables.
Collected the electric piano, workout bike and computer station and never tied specialty items to time.
Never mentioned traffic or explained the Houston 77007 to Spring 77386 drive as billable time — she charged the $105/truck travel fee but did not connect the distance to hours.
No equivalents or reference points (school bus, etc.) to make the estimate concrete.
Took the customer's name ('Janna Joyner') and then never used it once — said 'ma'am' throughout instead.
Long dead-end detour hunting the make, model and weight of the electric piano; it ended with an unusable transcript value and no decision, burning several minutes of a 19.8-minute call.
top_strength: The pricing and differentiator block is near-textbook and the best thing on this call. She hit the 'pricing is super simple' opener, the $95/hour per-mover rate with the Tuesday/Thursday best-value tiers volunteered unprompted, the honest $105-per-truck travel fee with the reason ('that second location falls outside our free service area'), and then all three differentiators in sequence: No Worries at 'up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse' with the competitor contrast against 'the state mandated 60 cents per pound,' Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee ('if we can't make it in the time window that we arranged, we immediately start discounting'). Her opening probe was also genuinely good — 'What are your biggest concerns about moving? What are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?' followed by 'have you had bad experiences?' — which surfaced broken TVs and a mover stepping on the customer's kid, and she met that with real empathy. And her estimate math is clean: 5 movers, 2 trucks, 7-8 hours, $3,535 to $4,010 reconciles exactly against $95/mover plus $210 travel.
coaching_note: Therese, you did the hard part and dropped the easy part. Highest-leverage fix: you had a live yes and you turned it into a to-do. When the customer said 'My daughter is home right now she can do it,' the next words needed to be 'Perfect — I'm sending that link to 713-755-1835 right now, can you get her on in the next ten minutes while I stay on with you?' Same thing on the move itself: she said yes to both Wednesday and Thursday in the first minute and you never asked for it, on a move happening this week. Book the walkthrough on the call, and ask for the date — 'we have Wednesday, want me to lock that in? There's no deposit and no card needed to hold it.' Second priority: Save Your Ass, and on this call it was free money. Her stated number one concern was 'efficiency, timing' and she's already packed 140-180 boxes with street-only parking and a narrow townhome entry — that is the exact setup for 'here's how to shrink that seven-to-eight hours: get the loose stuff out of drawers, consolidate the kids' toys, pull the photos off the walls, and take a carload of the small stuff yourself. Every one of those cuts your bill. Does that make sense?' Third: you collected every time variable on the call — three stories, narrow entry, no driveway, the piano, a thirty-plus-minute drive to Spring — and explained none of them. Naming those is what makes a seven-to-eight hour range believable instead of scary. Last thing, and it's small: you asked for her name, wrote down Janna Joyner, and then said 'ma'am' for nineteen minutes. Use it. Scope note for the record: this routed to a virtual walkthrough, but I graded pricing, clock and estimate on merit rather than as out of scope because you actually delivered all three in full — this functioned as a complete sales call that ended in a walkthrough instead of a booking. I did hold you to Save Your Ass for the same reason.
phone_presence_notes: Real empathy in the right moment ('I'm so sorry to hear that, that's definitely a nightmare' on the broken TVs and the mover stepping on her kid) and a strong concerns-first opening, but heavy filler chains of 'Okay. Gotcha. Alright.', zero use of the customer's name, and the customer went monosyllabic through the entire pricing monologue.
